title: 1969 AHSME Problem 21
statement: If the graph of \(x^2+y^2=m\) is tangent to that of \(x+y=\sqrt{2m},\) then:

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: \(m\) may be any nonnegative real number

solutions.text:
The circle has radius \(\sqrt m.\) The distance from the origin to the line is \[ \frac{\lvert-\sqrt{2m}\rvert}{\sqrt{1^2+1^2}}=\sqrt m. \] Thus the line is tangent for every \(m\ge0\) (with the \(m=0\) case degenerate at the origin).

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: The circle has center the origin and radius \(\sqrt m\)
